title: Newly registered domains and classification delay in DNS Control

definition.statement: Zscaler categorizes domains newly registered within the last 30 days, or observed for the first time, as Newly Registered and Observed Domains (NROD) until a proper classification is available.

quotes: The Zscaler service categorizes domains that are newly registered within the last 30 days or observed for the first time as Newly Registered and Observed Domains (NROD) until a proper classification is available.

latency.statement: The NROD database updates periodically, so a domain takes about 2 to 36 hours to be classified as NROD (depending on whether it is newly registered, observed or newly revived), and the first-ever DNS request for such a domain may have no URL classification.

quotes: a latency of about 2 to 36 hours is expected for domains to be classified as NROD depending on whether the domain is newly registered, observed, or newly revived.
the URL classification might not be available for the first-ever DNS request for such domains due to propagation delays.

revived.statement: Newly Revived Domains are sites reactivated after a brief period of inactivity of about 10 days.

quotes: reactivated after a brief period of inactivity for about 10 days.

suspicious-lookup-prereq.statement: Enable Suspicious New Domains Lookup (Advanced Policy Settings) is a prerequisite for using the Newly Registered and Observed Domains and Newly Revived Domains categories in a policy rule.

quotes: feature is a prerequisite for using the Newly Registered and Observed Domains and Newly Revived Domains URL categories in a policy rule.

dns-criterion.statement: DNS Control rules select NROD through Request Categories and Response Categories; the predefined High-Risk DNS Categories rule uses Newly Registered and Observed Domains, Newly Revived Domains and Other Security in both, and Zscaler especially recommends blocking the NROD category.

quotes: Request Categories: Newly Registered and Observed Domains, Newly Revived Domains, and Other Security are selected.
Blocking the Newly Registered and Observed Domains (NRODs) category is especially recommended.

nrod-attack-chains.statement: Zscaler says NRODs are often part of attack chains, such as termination points for DNS exfiltration through tunneling or hosts for drive-by malware before the domain is classified.

quotes: NRODs are often part of attack chains

nrod-latency-url-filtering.title: Whether the NROD classification latency applies equally to URL Filtering
nrod-latency-url-filtering.blocks: promising how fast a new domain is blockable in web policy
nrod-latency-url-filtering.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "The same NROD latency applies to URL Filtering." The latency statement is on the DNS Control page and is about the NROD database; no captured URL Filtering page states a latency. Register a test domain and time when each module classifies it.
